A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Distributionally Robust Causal Abstractions by the same authors. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable matching despite substantial expansion and reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original SLC and LiLUCAS experiments, including distribution shifts, structural misspecification, and intervention-map corruption in Section 5 and Appendix A.7.

after.justification: v2 retains those experiments and adds original nLUCAS, battery-manufacturing, and cMNIST evaluations and analyses in Section 5 and Appendix A.8.

M1.justification: v1 develops optimization for linear SCMs using mixing matrices. v2 adds a general additive-noise formulation using deterministic components D, abduced residuals U, shared observational residuals, and adversarial residual perturbations (Section 4, Appendices A.5/A.9, Algorithm 5). The abstraction map remains linear, and the earlier linear algorithms are retained.

E1.justification: Beyond the retained SLC/LiLUCAS experiments, v2 adds nonlinear-model learning on nLUCAS, real electric-battery manufacturing data, and cMNIST pixel-to-latent abstraction with rotation and lighting shifts. Training on nonlinear nLUCAS is distinct from v1's nonlinear test-time misspecification experiments.

E2.justification: The comparator roster remains BARY, GRAD, AbsLinp, and AbsLinn. However, v2 explicitly adapts BARY for general ANMs by averaging deterministic components and combining them with residuals, replacing the linear variant's averaging of mixing matrices (Appendix A.9.2, Algorithm 2). Existing linear comparisons retain their comparators.

E3.justification: v2 introduces shared-versus-independent-noise evaluation for nLUCAS, a 90/10 split for EBM, and cMNIST evaluation with pixel-only perturbations, relative error, and ground-truth-based test-time recentering. Empirical evaluation is also described as squared Frobenius error rather than v1's Frobenius distance; unchanged retained tables do not establish that those experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v2 adds the nLUCAS consistency/generalization control (Tables 11–12), cMNIST rotation and lighting robustness tests, and latent-space PCA and intervention-geometry analyses (Figures 11–12). The original radius sweeps, alternative-noise tests, and structural/intervention-map misspecification analyses remain in the appendix.

E5.justification: Mean-plus-standard-deviation reporting and paired t-tests are retained. v2 corrects the main-text threshold from p >= 0.05 to p < 0.05, matching v1's appendix, but omits v1's explicit statement of 100 random trials for misspecification results. This changes reporting without establishing a change in run counts.

E6.justification: The original numerical results are retained: v1 Tables 3–6 match v2 Tables 7–10. Substantial new results appear in v2 Tables 11–16. For example, Table 11 reports clean, independent-noise nLUCAS error of 8.98 ± 0.10 for DiRoCA4,4 versus 16.39 ± 0.13 for GRAD. These are new evaluations, not improvements over corresponding v1 scores.

T1.justification: v2 adds the worst-case error bound in Theorem 4.2/A.5, inner-maximization and convexity lemmas, an identity-coupling proposition, and general-ANM derivations. The original concentration results and proofs remain. The new Lemma A.3 asserts an exact maximum, although its norm-bound argument does not establish simultaneous attainment of the required bounds.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution statement, and conclusion add quantitative worst-case abstraction-error guarantees. The introduction also broadens the learning contribution to general additive-noise SCMs, beyond v1's linear-model development. The central distributionally robust causal-abstraction framework remains the same.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantive explanations involving structural estimation errors absorbed into residuals, GRAD overfitting shared noise realizations, and cMNIST robustness attributed to stable linear geometry. These extend v1's implicit-regularization explanation. Limitations concerning linear abstraction maps, known DAGs, and intervention mappings remain.

D1.justification: v2 supplies explicit intervention-map tables, detailed ANM estimation and abduction procedures, EBM residual centering, and cMNIST U-Net/FiLM and regularized cell-means implementations. It also adds general-method pseudocode and changes the listed code repository from DiRoCA to GenDiroca. These substantially expand v1's implementation documentation.

R1.justification: v2 adds Cohen et al. (2019), Altamirano et al. (2024), and Schneider et al. (2025), connecting its guarantees and mechanism-shift interpretation to robustness research. Separate Locatello (2019) and Peters (2016) references disappear. The central positioning between exact and uniform causal abstractions remains unchanged.

P1.justification: The introduction, optimization narrative, and experimental discussion are substantially rewritten. Optimization now leads with the general ANM formulation before linear special cases; the Gaussian concentration theorem moves out of the main text. The appendix replaces its contents list with a prose roadmap and introduces a more developed dataset subsection structure.

P2.justification: The main text and references switch from one column to two. Framework and roadmap diagrams are redesigned, the main robustness figure is recomposed, and new intervention tables, dataset diagrams, image examples, and analysis plots are added. Original result tables and robustness curves remain available in the appendix.

improvement.justification: v2 addresses v1's narrow synthetic evaluation with nonlinear, real-data, and image experiments, useful controls, and fuller implementation information. However, central additions have unresolved theoretical problems: Lemma A.3's exact-maximum claim is generally false, although the upper bound survives, and Algorithm 5 freezes D while Appendix A.5 describes propagating perturbed noise through nonlinear mechanisms. These issues affect the claimed general-ANM robustness contribution, preventing a confident net judgment between broader empirical support and weakened theoretical reliability.
